title: QueueFlux Scenario v1
description: Schema for QueueFlux simulation scenario files (schemaVersion 1).

schemaVersion.description: Must be 1. A breaking change to the scenario format requires a new schema version.

durationMicros.description: Total virtual simulation time in microseconds.

seed.description: Root random seed; identical seeds produce identical results.

queues.description: One or more queue definitions. Each queue must have exactly one worker pool and at least one workload.

workerPools.description: One or more worker-pool definitions. Currently exactly one pool per queue is supported.

workloads.description: One or more workload definitions. Multiple workloads may target the same queue.

id.description: Unique queue identifier within this scenario.

maxDepth.description: Maximum number of jobs waiting for a worker slot. Jobs exceeding this limit are rejected.

discipline.description: Order in which waiting jobs are dispatched to workers.

retryPolicy.description: Retry rules for transient processing failures. Omit to disable retries.

rateLimit.description: Global token-bucket rate limiter for job starts on this queue. Omit for unlimited.

SchedulingDiscipline.description: FIFO dispatches jobs in arrival order; PRIORITY dispatches highest-priority jobs first.

RetryPolicy.description: Exponential back-off retry policy. maxAttempts: 1 disables retries.

maxAttempts.description: Total number of attempts including the first. 1 disables retries.

initialBackoffMicros.description: Delay before the first retry in microseconds.

maxBackoffMicros.description: Upper bound on the exponential back-off delay in microseconds. Must be >= initialBackoffMicros.

multiplier.description: Exponential multiplier applied to the backoff after each failed attempt.

jitterFraction.description: Symmetric deterministic jitter fraction applied to each backoff interval.

RateLimitPolicy.description: Token-bucket rate limiter applied globally to job starts on one queue.

ratePerSecond.description: Token refill rate in jobs per second. 0 disables rate limiting.

burstCapacity.description: Maximum token count and initial bucket fill. Must be >= 1 even when rate limiting is disabled.

id.description: Unique worker-pool identifier within this scenario.

queueId.description: ID of the queue this pool drains.

workerCount.description: Number of workers in the pool.

concurrencyPerWorker.description: Number of jobs each worker can process simultaneously.

serviceTime.description: Distribution governing how long each job takes to process.

failureProbability.description: Probability that any single processing attempt fails transiently. Default 0.

outages.description: Planned intervals during which some workers stop accepting new jobs.

ServiceTimeModel.description: Service-time distribution for jobs processed by a worker pool.

constantMicros.description: Fixed service time in microseconds. Required when distribution is CONSTANT.

meanMicros.description: Mean service time in microseconds. Required when distribution is EXPONENTIAL or LOGNORMAL.

stdDevMicros.description: Standard deviation of the service time in microseconds. Required when distribution is LOGNORMAL.

ServiceDistribution.description: CONSTANT uses a fixed duration; EXPONENTIAL samples from a memoryless distribution; LOGNORMAL samples a right-skewed distribution from a real-space mean and standard deviation.

id.description: Unique workload identifier within this scenario.

queueId.description: ID of the queue jobs are submitted to.

startMicros.description: Virtual time at which this workload begins generating jobs.

endMicros.description: Virtual time at which this workload stops generating jobs. Must be > startMicros and <= durationMicros.

arrivals.description: Arrival process governing how frequently jobs appear.

priority.description: Job priority for PRIORITY-discipline queues. Higher values dispatch first. Default 0.

ratePerSecond.description: Average job arrival rate in jobs per second. Must be > 0.

ArrivalMode.description: CONSTANT produces perfectly spaced arrivals; POISSON produces exponentially distributed inter-arrivals.

WorkerOutage.description: A planned interval during which some workers stop accepting new jobs.

id.description: Unique outage identifier within the worker pool.

startMicros.description: Virtual time at which the outage begins.

endMicros.description: Virtual time at which the outage ends. Must be > startMicros.

unavailableWorkers.description: Number of workers in the pool that stop accepting new jobs during this interval.
